issues.description:
Method: Milkable.messageOnMilk
What problem statement/UML say: The UML and textual description in problem_statement.md declare messageOnMilk() as a no-argument abstract method that returns a String (e.g., "messageOnMilk():String") and the text says: "The method messageOnMilk() should return '[Animal Type] [name] is milked'". The template Main.java also calls m.messageOnMilk() with no arguments. What the solution says: solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java declares messageOnMilk(double volume) (a single double parameter) and Seal/Goat implement messageOnMilk(double volume). How this blocks students: This parameter mismatch is a compile-time/API incompatibility — the template and problem statement expect a no-arg method while the provided solution API requires a double parameter. Students following the problem text or using the template Main will find calls that do not match the solution signatures and will be unable to compile or will be confused which signature is canonical.
issues.suggestedFix:
Align the Milkable.messageOnMilk signature across all artifacts. Two viable resolutions (choose one to preserve pedagogical intent):

Option A (recommended to match problem text and template): Change the solution to a no-argument method returning String. Update solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java to declare "String messageOnMilk();". Update Seal and Goat to implement "public String messageOnMilk()" and return the string "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (e.g., "Seal Clarabelle is milked"). Ensure any example calls (Main.java) use the no-arg form.

Option B (if volume is intended): Update the problem statement, UML, and the template to require and document messageOnMilk(double volume). Modify problem_statement.md to describe the parameter and example return format (e.g., "Seal Clarabelle is milked (0.5L)"), update the UML to show messageOnMilk(double):String, and change the template Main.java to call m.messageOnMilk(someVolume) accordingly.

Either fix will resolve the compile-time/API incompatibility and remove student confusion; prefer Option A if the written spec and template are authoritative.

issues.description: The concept is the milk-action message method. In the problem statement (UML and textual tasks) the method is declared/expected as a no-argument method returning a String: "messageOnMilk(): String" (problem_statement.md shows the UML declaration and Part 2 instructions that expect a return like "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). The template Main calls this no-argument method (Main.java calls m.messageOnMilk()). In the solution repository, the Milkable interface and implementations use a different signature: messageOnMilk(double volume) returning String (Milkable.java and Seal/Goat implementations). Because the method name is identical but the parameter list differs, students following the template/problem will call m.messageOnMilk() and the solution's signature will not match, causing compilation errors and preventing a clear mapping between the required API in the exercise and the solution code.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution to match the problem/template: declare Milkable.messageOnMilk() as a no-argument method returning String (i.e., String messageOnMilk();), and update Seal.java and Goat.java to implement public String messageOnMilk() returning exactly the expected text (e.g., "Seal <name> is milked" and "Goat <name> is milked"). Alternatively, if the exercise should require a volume parameter, update the problem statement UML, textual instructions, and template Main to call and describe messageOnMilk(double volume) — but prefer the first option to preserve the current problem wording and template usage.
